title: Warm Moroccan Fish Tagine
description: A pungent and springy one-pot Moroccan dish featuring duck fat and cured ingredients, pescatarian-friendly and cooked in a donabe vessel.
instructions: Heat the duck fat in the donabe over medium heat.
Add the sliced onion and cook until it is translucent and starting to caramelize.
Add the minced garlic and grated ginger and cook for 1 minute.
Add the diced cured lemon, olive oil, cod fillets, chicken broth, dried apricots, and preserved olives.
Stir gently to combine and bring the mixture to a simmer.
Reduce the heat to low and cook, covered, for 20 minutes or until the fish is cooked through.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve the tagine hot, garnished with fresh parsley or cilantro.
Note: this recipe is for refrigerator pickling/preserving only — store in the refrigerator and consume within 1 week. Do not water-bath can without an acid (vinegar or lemon juice).
